deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is folio 13v (marked '2.') of Gauss's drafts on curved surfaces. The previous page sets up a surface x(t,θ) with linear element P dt² + 2Q dt dθ + R dθ², and a curve t(u), θ(u) on it. Along the curve the absolute curvature σ/s splits into a normal part (σ/s)cosψ and a 'Seitenkrümmung' (σ/s)sinψ. The latter is the modern geodesic curvature. This page computes it, first for a coordinate line θ = const and then for a general curve.

Notation on this page. a, b, c = ∂(x,y,z)/∂t and α, β, γ = ∂(x,y,z)/∂θ; these are not unit vectors. A prime means ∂/∂t; on P, Q, R a double prime means ∂/∂θ. Then P = a·a, Q = a·α, R = α·α. The unit normal is (X,Y,Z) = (a×α)/σ with σ = √(PR−Q²), consistent with the previous page's σX = bγ−cβ.

Part 1: the line θ = const, with t as parameter.
(1) s² = P and sξ = a etc., so ξ is the unit tangent. Differentiating gives a·a' = s s', i.e. s s' = ½P'.
(2) a' = σ s ξ' + s' ξ (componentwise). Here, as on the previous page, σ temporarily denotes the curvature magnitude, dξ/dt = σξ', and ξ' is the unit principal normal.
(3) Crossing (2) with ξ gives ξ×a' = σ s (ξ×ξ') = σ s ξ'', with ξ'' the binormal (η c' − ζ b' = σ s ξ'' etc.). This is correct.
(4) Now σ = |a×α| = √(PR−Q²). From X = (bγ−cβ)/σ etc. one gets the x-component of N×ξ:
 Yζ − Zη = [(a·a)α − a(a·α)]/(σ s).
 Check: (cα−aγ)c − (aβ−bα)b = α(b²+c²) − a(bβ+cγ) = Pα − Qa. This is correct.
(5) The lateral (geodesic) curvature is κ_g = (dξ/ds)·(N×ξ). Since ξ ⟂ N×ξ, this equals (1/s²) a'·(N×ξ). The page writes this as
 P(α·a') − Q(a·a') = σ s³ · Maass der Seitenkr.
(6) Two identities are needed:
 - a·a' = ½∂P/∂t.
 - α·a' = ∂Q/∂t − a·∂α/∂t = ∂Q/∂t − ½∂P/∂θ. Gauss writes ∂Q/∂t = a'α + b'β + c'γ + ½∂P/∂u; here u is a slip for θ (the later notation P'' confirms this).
 Hence κ_g = [P(Q' − ½P'') − ½QP']/(σ P^{3/2}).
(7) The element of lateral curvature is dκ = κ_g s dt. This gives
 (P(Q'−½P'') − ½QP') dt = σ·ss·d(Seitenkr.)
 and so
 d(Seitenkr.) = (PQ' − ½PP'' − ½QP') dt / (√(PR−QQ)·P).
 In modern terms this is κ_g(v=const) = (2EF_u − EE_v − FE_u)/(2√(EG−F²) E^{3/2}) = √(EG−F²) Γ²₁₁/E^{3/2}.

Part 2: a general curve t(u), θ(u), separated by a rule. Here t', θ' are d/du; P', Q', R' are ∂/∂t and P'', Q'', R'' are ∂/∂θ. The prefactor is s² σ = (Pt'²+2Qt'θ'+Rθ'²)√(PR−QQ); it is written and partly struck, and is completed on the next page as ssσ ∂f/∂u. Here df is the element of lateral curvature, df = κ_g s du. The result is
 ssσ df/du = (t'θ''−θ't'')(PR−QQ)
 + ½(Pt'+Qθ')(−P''t'² + 2Q't'² + 2R't'θ' + R''θ'²)
 − ½(Qt'+Rθ')(P't'² + 2P''t'θ' + 2Q''θ'² − R'θ'²).
This is the general geodesic-curvature formula in terms of E, F, G and their derivatives:
 κ_g s³ √(EG−F²) = W²(u'v''−u''v') + Σ_{ij} u^i' u^j' [Γ_{ij,2}(Eu'+Fv') − Γ_{ij,1}(Fu'+Gv')].
Expanding the Christoffel symbols of the first kind reproduces Gauss's brackets exactly. Setting θ' = 0 and t' = 1 recovers the Part-1 formula.
errors: Notational clash: σ denotes the curvature magnitude in σsξ' + ξs' = a' and σsξ'', but √(PR−QQ) (the area factor |r_t×r_θ|) from the Yζ−Zη line onward. The final formulas use the second meaning consistently, so no wrong result follows.
In ∂Q/∂t = a'α+b'β+c'γ + ½∂P/∂u the 'u' should be θ; it is a letter slip, and the next line correctly uses P'' = ∂P/∂θ.
The line '= σσsss·ψ' after the struck (Pα−Qa)a' is an abandoned or partly struck normalization. The retained statement '= σs³·Maass der Seitenkr.' is the correct one.

The final formula was checked against the standard Christoffel-symbol form and is correct, including the sign of t'θ''−θ't''. The next page shows Gauss first wrote (t''θ'−θ''t') and then corrected it.

results.what: Geodesic curvature of the coordinate curve θ = const: (PQ_t − ½PP_θ − ½QP_t)/(√(PR−Q²) P^{3/2}); element dκ = (PQ_t − ½PP_θ − ½QP_t)dt/(√(PR−Q²) P)
results.modern_name: Geodesic curvature of a parameter line, κ_g = √(EG−F²)Γ²₁₁/E^{3/2}
results.usually_credited_to: Minding (1830, concept of geodesic curvature); Bonnet (1848, 'courbure géodésique', formulas); Liouville (1850)

results.what: General formula for the geodesic curvature of a curve t(u), θ(u) purely in terms of P, Q, R, their first derivatives, and t', θ', t'', θ''
results.modern_name: Intrinsic (Bonnet/Liouville-type) formula for geodesic curvature in terms of the first fundamental form, showing its bending invariance

results.what: Expression of N×T in terms of the coordinate tangents: s σ (N×T) = Pα − Qa for the line θ = const
α·r_tt = Q_t − ½P_θ and a·r_tt = ½P_t
results.modern_name: Christoffel symbols of the first kind
results.usually_credited_to: Christoffel 1869 (notation); the content is in Gauss's Disquisitiones 1827

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's notion of 'Seitenkrümmung' and his Gauss–Bonnet-type considerations in the 1820s Nachlass are known to historians through Werke VIII and the 1825 'Neue allgemeine Untersuchungen'. However, a fully worked intrinsic formula for geodesic curvature of an arbitrary curve in E, F, G is usually attributed to Bonnet and Liouville around 1848–50, with Minding in 1830. A verified explicit general formula here is a notable but not revolutionary unpublished detail.
